description: REQ-005's edge case for the most dangerous crash window ('Process crashes immediately after broadcasting Leg 1 but before writing confirmed to the ledger') mandates recovery by having the next run 'query the chain for the actual tx status by the previously-recorded (pre-confirmation) tx hash/nonce.' This recovery mechanism REQUIRES that a tx hash/nonce was already durably written to disk before the crash. But PROP-009 (verification-architecture.md:47) explicitly claims to cover a THIRD, strictly earlier crash-injection point: 'post-broadcast-pre-ledger-write.' By definition, in that exact window, broadcast has returned a tx hash but NOTHING has yet been written to the ledger -- so there is no 'previously-recorded tx hash' for the next run to query by. REQ-005 never specifies how recovery works when even the pre-confirmation record itself was never persisted (e.g., via deterministic nonce reconstruction, or an on-chain 'list recent txs from source address' query independent of any local record). As written, PROP-009 asserts a guarantee ('never more than one confirmed-producing broadcast call per leg index') across a crash window for which REQ-005 supplies no implementable recovery strategy. An implementer following REQ-005's letter (query by previously-recorded hash) will find nothing recorded in this exact window and, per REQ-005's 'resume from the first unconfirmed leg' EARS clause, will re-broadcast Leg 1 -- causing an actual on-chain double-spend on Base and/or a duplicate IBC transfer-out. This makes PROP-009 as specified either unsatisfiable or falsely-passing (a test author would have to invent an unwritten mechanism to make it pass, and a different implementer could invent a different, unsafe one).

evidence.snippet: Process crashes immediately after broadcasting Leg 1 but before writing `confirmed` to the ledger: on the next run, the system MUST query the chain for the actual tx status by the previously-recorded (pre-confirmation) tx hash/nonce BEFORE deciding to resubmit

fix: Split REQ-005's crash taxonomy into the three windows PROP-009 actually claims to test, and specify a concrete, implementable recovery strategy for EACH: (1) pre-broadcast crash -> safe to resubmit (nothing sent). (2) post-broadcast-pre-ledger-write crash -> REQUIRE the broadcast call itself (BaseSigner.signAndBroadcast / the effectful wrapper) to durably and synchronously persist a 'submitting' record containing the deterministic sender nonce (not just a returned tx hash, which can be lost) BEFORE the broadcast RPC call is even made, so recovery can always re-derive an on-chain query key (address+nonce) regardless of whether the process died before or after the RPC returned. (3) post-ledger-write-pre-confirm crash -> query by the now-durable tx hash, as already specified. Update PROP-009's description to name this synchronous pre-broadcast nonce-record write explicitly, so the property test can actually exercise a well-defined mechanism instead of an unspecified one.
